narrator.name: Narrator
narrator.note: Tells the story of Abraham; steady and grave.

the-lord.name: The Lord
the-lord.note: God speaking to Abraham and others; majestic, calm, sovereign.

abraham.name: Abraham
abraham.note: The patriarch (Abram until 17:5), near a hundred years old; reverent, hospitable, bold yet humble in pleading.

sarah.name: Sarah
sarah.note: Abraham's wife (Sarai until 17:15), aged and barren; aggrieved in ch. 16, incredulous then afraid in ch. 18.

1.t: And the Lord appeared to him in the vale of Mambre as he was sitting at the door of his tent, in the very heat of the day.

2.t: And when he had lifted up his eyes, there appeared to him three men standing near to him: and as soon as he saw them, he ran to meet them from the door of his tent, and adored down to the ground.

3.t: Lord, if I have found favour in thy sight, pass not away from thy servant.

4.t: But I will fetch a little water, and wash ye your feet, and rest ye under the tree.

5.t: And I will set a morsel of bread, and strengthen ye your heart, afterwards you shall pass on: for therefore are you come aside to your servant.

6.t: Abraham made haste into the tent to Sara, and said to her:
Make haste, temper together three measures of flour, and make cakes upon the hearth.

7.t: And he himself ran to the herd, and took from thence a calf, very tender and very good, and gave it to a young man, who made haste and boiled it.

8.t: He took also butter and milk, and the calf which he had boiled, and set before them: but he stood by them under the tree.

9.t: And when they had eaten, they said to him:
Lo she is in the tent.

10.t: I will return and come to thee at this time, life accompanying, and Sara, thy wife, shall have a son.
Which when Sara heard, she laughed behind the door of the tent.

11.t: Now they were both old, and far advanced in years, and it had ceased to be with Sara after the manner of women.

12.t: After I am grown old, and my lord is an old man, shall I give myself to pleasure?
12.q: said secretly to herself; given to Sarah's voice

13.t: And the Lord said to Abraham:
Why did Sara laugh, saying: Shall I, who am an old woman, bear a child indeed?

14.t: Is there any thing hard to God? According to appointment I will return to thee at this same time, life accompanying, and Sara shall have a son.

15.t: for she was afraid. But the Lord said:

16.t: And when the men rose up from thence, they turned their eyes towards Sodom: and Abraham walked with them, bringing them on the way.

17.t: Can I hide from Abraham what I am about to do:

18.t: Seeing he shall become a great and mighty nation, and in him all the nations of the earth shall be blessed?

19.t: For I know that he will command his children, and his household after him, to keep the way of the Lord, and do judgment and justice: that for Abraham's sake, the Lord may bring to effect all the things he hath spoken unto him.

20.t: The cry of Sodom and Gomorrha is multiplied, and their sin is become exceedingly grievous.

21.t: I will go down and see whether they have done according to the cry that is come to me; or whether it be not so, that I may know.

22.t: And they turned themselves from thence, and went their way to Sodom: but Abraham as yet stood before the Lord.

23.t: Wilt thou destroy the just with the wicked?

24.t: If there be fifty just men in the city, shall they perish withal? and wilt thou not spare that place for the sake of the fifty just, if they be therein?

25.t: Far be it from thee to do this thing, and to slay the just with the wicked, and for the just to be in like case as the wicked; this is not beseeming thee: thou who judgest all the earth, wilt not make this judgment.

26.t: And the Lord said to him:
If I find in Sodom fifty just within the city, I will spare the whole place for their sake.

27.t: Seeing I have once begun, I will speak to my Lord, whereas I am dust and ashes.

28.t: What if there be five less than fifty just persons? wilt thou for five and forty destroy the whole city:
I will not destroy it, if I find five and forty.

29.t: And again he said to him:
But if forty be found there, what wilt thou do?
I will not destroy it for the sake of forty.

30.t: be not angry, I beseech thee, if I speak: What if thirty shall be found there?
I will not do it, if I find thirty there.

31.t: I have once begun, I will speak to my Lord: What if twenty be found there?
I will not destroy it for the sake of twenty.

32.t: be not angry, Lord, if I speak yet once more: What if ten shall be found there?
I will not destroy it for the sake of ten.

33.t: And the Lord departed, after he had left speaking to Abraham: and Abraham returned to his place.
